beginner.headline: Breaking Bad Actor RJ Mitte Dies at 34
beginner.brief: US actor RJ Mitte has died at the age of 34. He played the son of Walter White in the drama series Breaking Bad. Mitte lived with cerebral palsy. He worked to help people with disabilities. He created a foundation to support his community. Police confirmed his death, but they do not know the cause yet. One actor from the show shared a kind message about his friend.

intermediate.headline: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies at age 34
intermediate.brief: US actor RJ Mitte, who was best known for playing the defiant son of a drug kingpin in the television drama Breaking Bad, has died at the age of 34. The local police department confirmed his death, stating that no foul play is suspected and their investigation remains ongoing. Like his character on the show, Mitte lived with cerebral palsy and drew on his own personal experience for the role. His representative described the young man as a beloved philanthropist and a passionate advocate for disability rights. Mitte used his fame to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with health conditions. Bryan Cranston, who played his on-screen father, posted a tribute expressing deep despair over the tragic news. Cranston noted that the teen was quite raw when they started shooting the pilot episode in 2007, but he gradually grew into a fine performer. After achieving sudden fame, Mitte continued to fight for more varied roles and complex depictions of characters with disabilities on screen.

advanced.headline: Breaking Bad Actor RJ Mitte Dies Aged 34
advanced.brief: US actor RJ Mitte, best known for his compelling portrayal of Walter White Jr in the drama series Breaking Bad, has died aged 34. His representative expressed profound sadness over the tragic passing of the beloved performer and disability rights campaigner. A local justice of the peace stated that a post-mortem examination would be performed to establish the exact details of his death. As his on-screen father descended deeper into the criminal underbelly, Mitte's character frequently expressed his displeasure with memorable levity. His character's condition was based on a more serious case experienced by a late friend of the show's creator. Colleagues noted that Mitte brought essential authenticity to the role before building a public platform focused on inclusion. He also supported various philanthropic initiatives designed to challenge prevailing societal biases against people with disabilities. Bryan Cranston recalled meeting the young teenager, noting that Mitte approached his acting part with immense joy and enthusiasm. Cranston reflected on their friendship, which remained strong even after the intense media spotlight on the hit series dimmed. Co-star Aaron Paul shared that he was completely heartbroken by the news, describing himself as being at a loss.
